title: docs(plugin-charts): state the host-page font precondition for axis tick density
body:
Part of #9430
Clause-②: no

## What

This PR carries out ruling A on objectui#9430 (comment 5749199719, ratified by the maintainer in comment 5810715993): document the constraint, report it upstream, and make no code workaround.

It adds one section to `content/docs/plugins/plugin-charts.mdx`, titled **Axis Tick Labels and the Host Page Font**. The section:

- states the precondition: the host page's `body` font family must match the font the axis tick labels render with, or Recharts computes its tick-density and collision decisions against the wrong glyph metrics (labels overlap, or labels that would fit are dropped);
- says how to meet it;
- explains why it happens;
- names the in-repo instance by content: `ChartImpl` (the `bar-chart` type) sets `fontFamily: 'monospace'` in its y-axis `tick` props and gives that axis no `interval`.

No code, package or version changes.

**The upstream half is not in this PR.** This session cannot write to `recharts/recharts`. The upstream issue text is drafted in the dev report on objectui#9430 (JSON key `upstream_issue_draft`), and the maintainer will file it. That is why this PR says `Part of` and objectui#9430 remains open.

## Checked in the source

I read these in the worktree's installed `node_modules/recharts`, not in the docs:

- **Version.** `packages/plugin-charts/package.json` declares `recharts` `^3.10.1`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves it to 3.10.1, and the installed `package.json` reads 3.10.1. The page deliberately writes no version literal: `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` ratchets those, and AGENTS.md commandment 9 applies.
- **`es6/util/DOMUtils.js`.** `measureTextWithDOM` reuses one element with id `recharts_measurement_span`, created on first use by `document.body.appendChild`. Styles go on with `Object.assign(measurementSpan.style, SPAN_STYLE, style)`. `SPAN_STYLE` has no font-family key, so the span inherits its family from `body`. `createCacheKey` already has a `fontFamily` slot.
- **`es6/cartesian/CartesianAxis.js`.** The `layerRef` callback calls `window.getComputedStyle` on the first `recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value` node and copies only `computedStyle.fontSize` and `computedStyle.letterSpacing` into state. `fontFamily` is never read.
- **`es6/cartesian/getTicks.js`.**
  - A numeric `interval` returns before any measurement.
  - Otherwise every `getStringSize` call passes only `fontSize` and `letterSpacing`.
  - The measured dimension is `width` for a top or bottom orientation and `height` otherwise.
  - `tick` is read only as a truthiness guard.
- **`es6/component/Text.js`.** Word widths are measured with the `style` prop, not with a `fontFamily` attribute.
- **Y-axis default.** The default `interval` is `implicitYAxis.interval`, which is `'preserveEnd'` (`es6/state/selectors/axisSelectors.js`).
- **`ChartImpl.tsx` on `origin/main` `0651e7ab4`.** The `YAxis` tick props include `fontFamily: 'monospace'` and there is no `interval`. The `XAxis` uses the same font with `interval={0}`. `bar-chart` renders through `ChartBarRenderer`, which lazy-loads `ChartImpl`.

Measured here in real Chromium (a throwaway probe that copies `SPAN_STYLE` at 12px):

- The absolutely positioned span computes to `display: block`.
- Its width changes with the font family.
- Its height changes with the family only under `line-height: normal`: serif 15px, sans-serif 14px, monospace 14px. Under `line-height: 1.5` it is 18px for all three.

That measurement is the basis for the page's last sentence: `ChartImpl`'s vertical axis can keep a different set of labels only on a page that leaves `line-height` at `normal`.

Taken from the card, not re-measured: the earlier Chromium repro in which mismatched fonts changed the kept label count.

### One correction to the dispatch's wording

The dispatch described the in-repo instance as having its *width* measured against the host font. In the source, a vertical axis measures label *heights*: `getTicks` uses `height` when the orientation is not top or bottom. The page therefore says "measured in the page's body font" and names the height.

## README

`packages/plugin-charts/README.md` does not document axis ticks or fonts. Its only axis mentions are the `dataKey` / `xAxisKey` data-binding rows, so I left it untouched.
